To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intermediate beams in SPSW models should be designed to resist the forces determined by fully yielded plates and that the roof and foundation level beams should be designed according to CAN/CSA-S16-01.
intermediate beams in SPSWs should be designed for the maximum shear force imposed by the fully yielded plates.

the intermediate beams in SPSWs should not be designed to resist gravity loads only and that they should be designed for forces determined by the full strength of the plates, not just the strength of the plate at the ultimate limit state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of SPSW models that can resist seismic loads without the development of in-span plastic hinge in the intermediate beams.
the seismic response of SPSW models that are not designed according to the CAN/CS A S16-01.
the seismic behavior of the beams other than the roof and foundation ones, which are usually the most critical ones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in order to avoid in-span plastic hinges and to prevent excessive deformations of intermediate beams, it is necessary to design these beams according to criteria III or, alternatively, to use beams with larger flexural strength.

, in order to prevent in-span plastic hinges in SPSW models with intermediate beams designed according the ASCE 07 load combinations, the design should be based on the assumption that all plates are yielded, and the beam should be designed to resist the corresponding beam shear force.
the seismic design criteria currently adopted for intermediate beams in SPSWs are not adequate to avoid in-span plastic hinges.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current design provisions for intermediate beams of steel plate shear walls do not provide a sufficient level of ductility.
, for the design of intermediate beams in SPSWs, a strength level that is greater than that required by criteria I and II is needed.
the seismic behavior of SPSWs is strongly affected by the design of the intermediate beams.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the seismic behavior of SPSWs depends not only on the strength of the plates, but also on the strength of intermediate beams, which must be designed accordingly.
the strength levels needed to avoid in-span plastic hinges are significantly higher than the strength levels determined by the current design codes.

, to avoid the formation in-span plastic hinges in intermediate beams, the design strength of these beams needs to be at least 50 percent greater than the design strength of the foundation and roof beams.
